eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 106 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

code:
-- A table-level request needs to know:
-- "is a conflicting lock held ANYWHERE inside this table?"
-- Naively: scan every row. On millions of rows -- too slow.
caption: Intent locks exist to avoid exactly this scan.

eyebrow: A signal flag one level up
caption: IX says "an X lock exists somewhere below" — without naming where.

code:
-- IS  = Intent Shared:    an S lock exists below
-- IX  = Intent Exclusive: an X lock exists below
-- SIX = Shared on the whole table,
--       PLUS intent to take X locks within it
caption: A flag at the higher level, mirroring the real lock below.

code:
SELECT resource_type, request_mode
FROM sys.dm_tran_locks
WHERE request_session_id = @@SPID;
-- OBJECT / IX   <- table-level signal
-- KEY    / X    <- the actual row lock
caption: One row-level lock, one table-level intent lock announcing it.

subtitle: Protecting the table's structure, not its data.
